conventions.convention: The metric is diag(-1,1,1,1); x⁰=ct is measured in metres; μ and ωμ are inverse lengths. Physical energy is ℏcωμ and physical momentum is ℏk.
The future-shell measure is d³k/((2π)³2ωμ); μ≥0, and the massless apex is omitted. The Fourier phase is ωμx⁰−k·x.

The scalar symmetric-Fock and Dirac particle/antiparticle CAR-Fock assignments and zero-particle vacua are adopted physical assumptions, not a general spin-statistics theorem or empirical conclusion. Countable Choice is assumed.

Scalar local algebras use real compactly supported tests and bounded Weyl operators; Dirac local observable algebras use even products of bounded smeared fields and their adjoints. No pointwise field or coincident product is supplied.
Physical scalar momentum is P_s,j=ℏdΓ_s(k_j), whereas the mathematical positive-exponent spatial generator is G_s,j=dΓ_s(−k_j); thus P_s,j=−ℏG_s,j.
Bosonic ladder indices start at n=0. The annihilation formula at n=0 means a(h)|0⟩=0. The one-mode number operator uses the composition domain of a†(h)a(h).

For a normalized vector, operator means and variances require membership in D(A), without requiring D(A²). Measurement probabilities require an actually constructed normalized finite bounded instrument.

load_bearing.statement: Assign the real scalar species to the bosonic symmetric Fock representation and assign the Dirac field to the particle/antiparticle CAR representation on H₊⊕overline(H₋). Choose the zero-particle Fock vectors as the scalar and Dirac vacuum states. These are adopted model assignments; the fields are the specified smeared constructions.

Define the norm-closed scalar Weyl and even Dirac local observable algebras, vacuum vector states, and scalar and Dirac physical translation observables on their stated maximal domains. Means and variances are defined for normalized vectors in D(A). The charge-number expression is only a candidate definition; no self-adjointness or proved-domain claim is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice and the selected free model. For every unit scalar mode h, (a†(h))ⁿΩ_s/√(n!) are orthonormal finite-particle vectors satisfying the displayed creation/annihilation ladder and N_h|n⟩=n|n⟩. For every unit particle or antiparticle Dirac mode u, N_u=c†(u)c(u) is an orthogonal projection, c†(u)²=0, and its vacuum-generated one-mode subspace has occupations 0 and 1.

published_dependencies.used_for: The explicit choice hypothesis carried through every assigned item; its indexed and at-most-countable-family formulations match the batch's uses.
The prerequisite Fock convention reverses the repository's first-variable-linear pairing to a second-variable-linear pairing without changing the norm.
The completeness convention underlying the cited Hilbert and Fock constructions.
The Fock prerequisites use its completed Hilbert tensor products, product pairing and dense elementary tensor span under Countable Choice.
The Fock prerequisites use bounded tensor extensions for contractions and their norm bounds; it supplies no extension of unbounded maps.
The Fock prerequisites use its symmetric and antisymmetric orthogonal projections and vanishing of antisymmetrized repeated factors.

concerns.concern: The Conditional input section explicitly says the charge-number operator/domain is missing from the current MF04 carrier and calls the displayed expression a 'candidate definition conditional on that missing mathematical interface'. This is honestly qualified, and no downstream use inspected here promotes it to a theorem, but the charged-observable branch remains an unfinished prerequisite obligation. A finite-sector bounded self-adjoint operator/direct-sum argument appears sufficient to supply the missing interface, including q_SI=0.

In def-qft-dirac-projections, that multiplier's t is explicitly a length-coordinate increment and its phase is ωt, with ω in inverse metres. The physical-time notation needs an explicit ct conversion or a length-coordinate time label. The norm-divergence conclusion is unaffected, but the cited parameter convention is inconsistent as written.

The qft-f02 page frontmatter has no requires entry, although its prose says its deductions are conditional on the adopted QFT-F01 model, and its items explicitly depend on post-qft-free-field-model. The assigned seam is 'qft-f02 requires qft-f01'; the page prerequisite declaration does not currently record that edge.
